hints: Find $\Phi(0.5)$ and $\Phi(-1.167) = 1 - \Phi(1.167)$, then subtract the two cumulative probabilities.
walkthrough: Let $X$ denote the time in minutes taken to cook an egg: $X \sim \mathrm{N}(4.2, 0.6^2)$ with mean $\mu = 4.2$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 0.6$.

We need to find the probability that cooking time is between 3.5 and 4.5 minutes:
$$\mathrm{P}(3.5 < X < 4.5) = \mathrm{P}(X < 4.5) - \mathrm{P}(X < 3.5)$$

Standardise the upper limit $X = 4.5$:
$$Z_1 = \frac{4.5 - 4.2}{0.6} = \frac{0.3}{0.6} = 0.5$$
From the standard normal table:
$$\Phi(0.5) = 0.6915$$

Standardise the lower limit $X = 3.5$:
$$Z_2 = \frac{3.5 - 4.2}{0.6} = \frac{-0.7}{0.6} \approx -1.1667$$
By normal curve symmetry:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z < -1.167) = 1 - \Phi(1.167)$$
From the table, $\Phi(1.167) = 0.8784$, so:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z < -1.167) = 1 - 0.8784 = 0.1216$$

Subtract the lower tail from the upper tail:
$$\mathrm{P}(3.5 < X < 4.5) = 0.6915 - 0.1216 = 0.5699$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.570$.

hints: Note that 12% of people take more than $t$ minutes to cook an egg, meaning $\mathrm{P}(X > t) = 0.12$.
Look up $\Phi(z) = 0.88$ in the normal distribution table to find $z = 1.175$.
Set up the standardisation equation $\dfrac{t - 4.2}{0.6} = 1.175$ and solve for $t$.
walkthrough: We are given that $12\%$ of people take more than $t$ minutes to cook an egg: $\mathrm{P}(X > t) = 0.12$.

Convert this upper tail into a cumulative probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < t) = 1 - 0.12 = 0.88$$

Look up $0.88$ in the main body of the normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(1.17) = 0.8790, \quad \text{difference for } 5 \text{ is } 10 \implies \Phi(1.175) = 0.8800$$
So the standard score is:
$$z = 1.175$$

Write down the standardisation formula:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$$
Substitute $Z = 1.175$, $X = t$, $\mu = 4.2$, and $\sigma = 0.6$:
$$1.175 = \frac{t - 4.2}{0.6}$$

Add $4.2$ to both sides:
$$t = 4.2 + 0.705 = 4.905\text{ minutes}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $t = 4.91\text{ minutes}$.

hints: Recall from part (ii) that the probability of a person taking at most $t$ minutes is $\mathrm{P}(X \le t) = 0.88$.
For a sample of $n$ independent people, the probability that none of them takes more than $t$ minutes is $(0.88)^n$.
Set up the inequality $(0.88)^n < 0.003$ and take logarithms of both sides.
Remember to reverse the inequality sign when dividing by $\ln(0.88)$ (since it is negative), and round up to the next integer.
walkthrough:
From part (ii), we know that $88\%$ of people take at most $t$ minutes to cook an egg, while $12\%$ take more than $t$ minutes:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{takes } \le t) = 0.88$$

In a random sample of $n$ people, the probability that none of them takes more than $t$ minutes means that all $n$ people take at most $t$ minutes. Since people are independent, this probability is:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{none takes } > t) = (0.88)^n$$

We are required to find the smallest integer $n$ such that this probability is less than $0.003$:
$$(0.88)^n < 0.003$$

Take the natural logarithm (or base 10 log) of both sides:
$$\ln((0.88)^n) < \ln(0.003)$$
Use the power rule of logarithms:
$$n \ln(0.88) < \ln(0.003)$$

Divide both sides by $\ln(0.88)$. Crucially, because $\ln(0.88)$ is negative, the inequality sign flips:
$$n > \frac{-5.809143}{-0.127833}$$
Divide:
$$n > 45.44$$

Because $n$ must be an integer, round up to the smallest whole number greater than $45.44$:
$$n = 46$$
